name: Monarch Compute Campus
developer: Nscale (UK) via Monarch Cloud Campus LLC. Acquired AIPCorp from Fidelis New Energy / 8090 Industries, Mar 2026.

facts.v: Up to 2,250 acres. Phase 1: 1.35 GW of compute, $69.2B, 4,375 construction / 645 permanent jobs. Path to 8+ GW.
2.16 GW off-grid gas microgrid with 864 reciprocating engines, plus diesel backup.

Anthropic: GPU agreements worth up to approximately $44.6B, in four tranches at Monarch (Nscale S-1). TechCrunch reports the first is a 460 MW building. Microsoft's 1.35 GW letter of interest was never produced, and Bloomberg reported it walked away.
Daniel Shapiro (Nscale CPO), William Calhoun, Jason Bechtle (site mgr). Residents Kimberly Mattox, Stephanie Butcher, Joshua Jeffers. Mason WV United (Elaine Matheny).
Air permit R14-0042: written comments are due before 5 p.m. Nov 13, 2026 (DEP notice); no final decision yet. DEP violations for sediment and dust May through Aug. About 6 homes flooded May 23–24.

Building 1: $10B to $10.5B for the data center and power, about $1B of it spent by Sep 30, 2026, plus $21B to $22B for GPUs and other compute. No binding commitments yet for any of the financing the Anthropic agreements need (Nscale S-1/A, Nov 12).

latest.t: DEP's written comment period on the air permit closed Nov 13, with no date set for a final decision. Nscale's Nov 12 amended S-1 discloses that Anthropic exercised a right on Sep 29 to negotiate for Building 2, with 60 days to reach a deal.

history.t: Nscale buys AIPCorp; the Mason County site becomes an AI campus
Site work under way: DEP dust warning

timeline.t: The WV EDA approves a forgivable $62.5M loan to Fidelis subsidiary Mountaineer GigaSystem LLC for an earlier hydrogen plan on the site. $25M was paid out and the second tranche was waived.
Nscale acquires AIPCorp (American Intelligence & Power Corp.), a Fidelis New Energy / 8090 Industries affiliate.
Air permit R14-0042 application filed with the DEP.
DEP dust warning.
A silt-fence failure floods about 6 homes in Meadowlands Estates and on University Lane (May 23–24).
Hearing on stormwater permit WVR312628 for a 556.5-acre pipeline disturbance in Putnam and Mason.
Particulate violation letter from DAQ Director Laura Crowder.
Certified as a High Impact Data Center at the WV Chamber summit at The Greenbrier.
Nscale files for an IPO. Its S-1 discloses Anthropic agreements worth up to approximately $44.6B for GPU capacity at Monarch, and no binding financing commitments for the build yet.

Anthropic exercises its right to contract for more compute at Building 2 on the Monarch campus, opening 60 days (subject to mutual extension) to negotiate an agreement. If one is signed, Anthropic has 15 business days to exercise a similar right for Building 3 (Nscale S-1/A, Nov 12).

Bloomberg reports Nscale and Anthropic are in talks on a second deal, for a second 460 MW data center at the Monarch campus. The FT and CNBC reported it too, and the FT repeated it Nov 5 without naming the campus.
timeline.verify: The dollar value and 460 MW size still rest on unnamed sources. Nscale's Nov 12 S-1/A confirms only that Anthropic exercised a right to negotiate for Building 2 on Sep 29, and gives no value or size. Anthropic's Nov 17 S-1/A lists only the August agreements (up to approximately $44.6B).

timeline.t: DEP air-permit workshop at Point Pleasant High School.
DEP virtual public hearing on the air permit.
Nvidia is reported in talks to guarantee construction debt.
Nscale files an amended S-1; the price range is still blank.
Written comment period on air permit R14-0042 closes at 5 p.m.
DEP final decision on air permit R14-0042.

Building 2: Nscale and Anthropic sign an agreement, extend the 60-day window (which by our count runs out around Nov 28), or let it lapse. Nscale would then be free to contract Building 2 with someone else.
timeline.verify: The end date is our count of 60 days from Sep 29. The S-1/A does not say whether these are calendar days, and the window can be extended by mutual agreement.

sources.label: DEP: public comment and meetings, Monarch (notice dated 9/29/2026)

name: Project Tamarack
developer: Starwood Digital Ventures (Starwood Capital Group, Miami Beach). CEO Anthony Balestrieri.

Gov. Patrick Morrisey: "West Virginia electricity bills are not going up from these announcements. Period." Resident Kimberly Mattox lives a quarter mile away.

timeline.t: A Delaware board upholds the denial of Starwood's 1.2 GW "Project Washington."

A stormwater pollution prevention plan filed with the DEP for Starwood affiliate Tamarack Investment Holdings LLC covers six building pads, about 227 acres of disturbance, and estimates construction from Mar 1, 2027 to Apr 5, 2029.
timeline.verify: Only the Gazette-Mail has reported the plan; we have not opened the DEP filing. The dates are the plan's estimates.

DEP action on the stormwater construction permit, and whether work starts on the plan's estimated Mar 1, 2027 date.

name: Google Buffalo Campus
developer: Google, via affiliate Cumulus Group LLC.

facts.v: About 1,700 acres along Charleston Rd / WV-62, next to a 765 kV ApCo line. The Army Corps filing shows 8 buildings.
Grid. Google says it pays for power and for water/sewer upgrades. 288 diesel emergency generators and 128 cooling towers in the DEP air application (Jul 22).
34+ acres of wetlands and 45,000+ ft of streams affected. Projected 249 t/yr NOx.
Commission President Andy Skidmore. Putnam United (Heather Ransom, Jessica Lacy, Joseph DeGroff). Residents Melanie and Tim Lacy, Barbie Fronk, Ashley Armstrong, Dr. Kyle McCausland.

latest.t: The County Commission adopted a resolution saying data center developers should fund all water, sewer, and power upgrades. The DEP air permit application (R13-3782) is still pending, with no comment period posted.

history.t: Announced and certified

timeline.t: Gov. Morrisey announces the Google campus, already certified after six-plus months of closed-door meetings (revealed later by a Gazette-Mail FOIA).
Support and concern; the site sits next to a 765 kV ApCo line.
Putnam County residents speak out.
DEP air permit application: 288 diesel emergency generators and 128 cooling towers.
Putnam United brings a resolution to the County Commission asking for resident input.

The County Commission adopts its own data center resolution, written after Putnam United's. It says developers should fund 100 percent of water, sewer, and power upgrades. President Andy Skidmore said developers should follow county rules "as if House Bill 2014 didn't exist," and that Google is going through the county planning commission.
DEP preliminary determination and public comment period on air permit application R13-3782 (none posted yet).

name: Ridgeline (Fundamental Data)
developer: Fundamental Data LLC (Purcellville, VA). Responsible individual Casey Chapman. Counsel: Speaker Roger Hanshaw (Bowles Rice).

facts.v: Starts at 291 acres and could reach 10,000. Reporting has described up to 5.2 GW. Target: 2028.
About 785 MW gas plant with diesel backup (three 10M-gallon tanks). About 1.3 GW of solar floated.
Air Quality Board upheld the permit Feb 5. ICA dismissed appeals on jurisdiction Aug 26, and the groups say they will refile. The Commerce violation notice (Jun 18) was rescinded Jul 1.
Tucker United (Amy Margolies), WV Highlands Conservancy (Olivia Miller), Sierra Club WV. Davis Council voted 5-0 against. Sen. Randy Smith called opponents "vacation homeowners."

latest.t: WSAZ's "Davis V. Goliath" feature on Davis residents and tourism. The groups have not yet refiled their air-permit appeal at the Supreme Court of Appeals.

ICA Judges Daniel Greear and Charles Lorensen recuse. Chief Justice C. Haley Bunn appoints three replacements.
The Supreme Court of Appeals denies Fundamental Data's bid to skip the ICA.

The DEP accepts a redacted purchase agreement as proof of site control.
The ICA dismisses both appeals on jurisdiction, not on the merits. The groups say they will refile.
NPR national feature on dark skies, ski areas, and the Monongahela National Forest.
WSAZ feature "Davis V. Goliath" on Davis residents and tourism businesses. Gov. Morrisey: "Nothing's been approved."
Appeals refiled at the Supreme Court of Appeals, which the ICA said has jurisdiction over the final-permit appeal. None found as of Nov 18, 2026.

developer: Penzance (Washington, D.C.), via Bedington Owner LLC.

Grid-connected. No microgrid.
First certified "High Impact" project under HB 2014 (Feb 2026). DEP stormwater construction permit application (WVR 113565, 147.66 acres of Phase 1 grading) accepted Jul 2026.
Commission President Eddie Gochenour ("very optimistic"). No Data Centers in the Eastern Panhandle (Rupok Bhuiyan).

latest.t: The DEP told Berkeley County it must still meet its federal stormwater permit, including ordinances, across the area that covers the data center site. The AG had declined a related request Oct 9, citing the Barks lawsuit.

timeline.t: Gov. Morrisey announces WV's first certified "High Impact" data center: $4B, 548 acres, 600 MW.
The DEP accepts the stormwater construction permit application as complete (Jul 29–30).
Berkeley County asks the Attorney General how HB 2014 affects its stormwater duties.
AG J.B. McCuskey declines, citing the pending Barks lawsuit.
The DEP tells Berkeley County it remains bound by its federal MS4 stormwater permit, including stormwater ordinances, across the whole covered area. The county had asked on Aug 28.

Attorney Stephen New has named QTS as a target for future suits.

Natural gas and/or the grid, with geothermal cooling. The listing describes a closed-loop geothermal heat sink.
Redmond says the feasibility study is preliminary. The proposal has drawn criticism on social media.

name: Centre Foundry Data Center
developer: Silicon Foundation Energy, with Stokes Inc. (SC). Bought the 15-acre former Centre Foundry for $1.5M.

facts.v: Stated range of 10 MW, then 20–30 MW, then 100 MW. Later described as 50 MW, which is under HB 2014's 90 MW line and so subject to City of Wheeling review.
Grid plus gas backup. Closed-loop Ohio River water cooling.

Barks v. Silicon Foundation (Ohio Co. Circuit Court, Judge David Sims, filed Jul 2026): 12 residents challenge HB 2014's constitutionality and the site's zoning. The AG intervened to defend HB 2014. Silicon Foundation moved to dismiss (Sep 2026); no ruling reported.
Del. Shawn Fluharty (D-Ohio) held town halls at the Warwood Veterans Assn. and Waterfront Hall. Resident Amanda McWhorter (WVDCAP).

latest.t: Wheeling City Council heard the first reading of data center rules (Article 1365); a vote is expected Dec 1. Silicon Foundation's motion to dismiss Barks is pending before Judge David Sims.

history.t: Town halls against the project

timeline.t: Del. Shawn Fluharty holds a town hall at the Warwood Veterans Association. Stokes Inc. says the site will build modules for data centers.
Twelve Warwood residents file Barks v. Silicon Foundation in Ohio County Circuit Court (Judge David Sims), challenging HB 2014 and the site's zoning.
The project is revised to 50 MW, under the 90 MW HB 2014 line, so the City of Wheeling keeps review.
AG J.B. McCuskey moves to intervene to defend HB 2014's constitutionality. The court grants it.
Silicon Foundation moves to dismiss, arguing there is no ripe controversy. Judge Sims later denies the plaintiffs' request for 90 to 120 days of discovery. Response due Oct 28.

timeline.t: The AG's office cites Barks in declining Berkeley County's opinion request.
Wheeling City Council hears the first reading of Article 1365, data center rules for Industrial districts.
Wheeling City Council second reading and vote on Article 1365.

name: Project Country Roads
place: Boone Co. · north of Danville (former Hobet mine)
developer: LM Core Energy Services, Inc. (Houston). CEO Jarrette Lewis. Anticipated tenant named in the petition: TensorWave (Las Vegas).

facts.v: Certification notice: roughly 3,557 acres and about 1.4 GW of anticipated full-campus demand. An unsigned June 22 MOU: about 3,702 acres, $9.65 billion through the first phase, 2,000 to 3,000 peak construction jobs and 200 to 400 permanent. Other project documents: up to 10 GW and 8,000 acres.
facts.verify: All figures come from confidential documents described by one outlet (Gazette-Mail, Nov 7). The $9.65 billion is from an unsigned MOU, not a state announcement.

facts.v: MOU target: 50 MW initial power in Q4 2026, 1,000 MW commercial operation in Q4 2028, 10 GW buildout from 2026 through 2034. Investor deck: 400 MW by Q4 2027.
facts.verify: Company targets in unsigned and private documents, reported only by the Gazette-Mail.

facts.v: Petition: Appalachian Power issued a conceptual service plan in July and costs for the first 400 MW in August; 200 MW temporary service at 138 kV, then permanent 765 kV service from a new station cut into the Culloden-Wyoming line. The MOU also proposes on-site generation and energy storage. No fuel has been reported.
facts.verify: From the petition and MOU as reported by the Gazette-Mail. Appalachian Power declined to comment on the project.

Petition: on-site wastewater treatment plant discharging to the Little Coal River. Average and peak daily water use listed as 4,000 to 5,000 gallons per day.

name: Mt. Storm Combined Cycle Station
developer: Dominion Energy (Virginia Electric and Power Company, d/b/a Dominion Energy Virginia).

facts.v: About 2,600 MW of gas-fired combined-cycle generation (Dominion and the governor). Storm property, next to the 1.6 GW coal plant, which stays open.

facts.verify: We have not seen a DEP draft permit, public notice or comment period for R14-0043. Check the DEP DAQ notice page.

facts.v: More than 1,400 construction jobs and 150 permanent jobs, per the governor's office. Company officials estimate nearly $950 million in tax revenue for Grant County over the first 36 years.
